entries.english: Seven Days of the Week, Four Seasons, Lunar Months & 5-Year Sequence (Tutschek 1844)
entries.translation: 7 Days (torbanⁱ = week, p. 87; kurna = 10-day period, p. 38): 1. Gifti ('The Lady') or Kamiza (p. 60), 2. Djimada / Djimata (p. 80), 3. Zambata t'ina (preceded by cadame, pp. 40, 183), 4. Zambata guda (p. 183), 5. Zaño (p. 183), 6. Maczaño or Tafno (pp. 85, 161), 7. Arbi (p. 11) / 4 Seasons: birra (spring, ushered in mid-September when the yellow kelo flower blooms and celebrated with the Magzala / Maczala New Year feast on the duba hearth, pp. 34, 103, 114, 130, 135, 162), bona (summer, p. 139), arfaza (autumn/harvest, p. 11), ganna (winter/rainy season, p. 60) / Months: 1st hadoleza or hadami (p. 190 & Pt. II p. 75), 2nd hagayo (p. 189), 3rd wadabadji (p. 147), furma (p. 124) / 5-Year Relative Sequence (p. 131): barrakan (2 years ago) → barrengata (last year) → barrana (this year) → barragere (next year) → barratchanu (in 2 years)
entries.pronunciation: gif-ti, dji-ma-ta, zam-ba-ta t'i-na, zam-ba-ta gu-da, za-nyo, mac-za-nyo, ar-bi / bir-ra, bo-na, ar-fa-za, gan-na

entries.english: Divisions of the Day & Night in Tutschek (1844)
entries.translation: ganama aboro (very early dawn, p. 7) → ganama (sunrise to 8 a.m., p. 59) → dirama (8 to 10 a.m., p. 100) → ware (9 to 10 a.m., p. 148) → ware korate (forenoon before noon, p. 148) → oba / adun guba keza (noon, when calves are watered oba dyabi; afternoon hours counted oba lamuti, oba zaditi, oba afuriti, oba z'aniti, p. 23) → galgala (evening, p. 59) → wari (first night-watch, p. 148) → galgala dimemeza (midnight, p. 101)

entries.english: Complete Cattle Classification under Lon (Loni) in Tutschek (1844, p. 160 & Pt. II p. 20)
entries.translation: Male cattle: tshabi (newborn calf) → djibitcha (young bull-calf) → gorba (3-year-old steer) → wofana (young bullock) → godiyo (pl. godiyoni, gelded plough-ox) → korma (pl. koromi, breeding bull: korma bordeda with erect hump vs. korma gurra with hanging hump, p. 36) → ulfin → zanga (castrated fattened ox) / Female cattle: tshabi (calf) → rad'a / rada (2-year-old heifer) → goromza (breeding heifer) → zã / zawa (cow; zilga = pregnant/milk cow giving colostrum zilga; gua = weaned calf or cow dried up of milk) → dulatcha (aged cow destined for ceremonial offering)
entries.pronunciation: tsha-bi, dji-bit-cha, gor-ba, wo-fa-na, go-di-yo, kor-ma, ul-fin, zan-ga / ra-d'a, go-rom-za, za-wa, zil-ga, du-lat-cha

entries.english: Prayer 1 (Akafed'e's Prayer after the War of Hambo and Hamaya, 1845)
entries.translation: Wacayo laftana, goftako! ati na guba teza, ani zi dyalan taa. Ho haman nati d'ufe, aka mukni adu narra cabu, ati hama nati cabi, goftako, gadiza na tai! Wacayo, goftako, biftun cara zodoma, ho dini d'ufe ramoke lafati hin adjezizin, ira cabi!
entries.pronunciation: wa-ca-yo laf-ta-na gof-ta-ko a-ti na gu-ba te-za
entries.context: Karl & Lawrence Tutschek (1845, pp. 84–87, Prayer 1 vv. 1–16 — 'Good God of this earth, my Lord! Thou art above me, I am below thee... be thou my shadow! Thou Sun with thirty rays...')

entries.translation: Ya Waca nagan na bultshite nagan na oltshi. Ede inand'aca karakora kan naga naf god'te, ya Waca, milkiko na gadyêlzi... zi wamad'etan ola, gofta goftan cabne.
entries.pronunciation: ya wa-ca na-gan na bul-tshi-te na-gan na ol-tshi
entries.context: Karl & Lawrence Tutschek (1845, pp. 87–88, Morning Prayer — 'O God, thou hast let me pass the night in peace, let me pass the day in peace... lead my steps... O Lord, who hast no Lord!')

entries.translation: Ya Waca nagan na oltshite, nagan na bultshi, gofta goftan cabne; zi male dyaban hindyiru, tokitchi gidin cabne. Harkake dyaladan ola, harkake dyaladan bula, had'ikozi, abankozi.
entries.pronunciation: ya wa-ca na-gan na ol-tshi-te na-gan na bul-tshi
entries.context: Karl & Lawrence Tutschek (1845, p. 88, Evening Prayer — 'O God, thou hast let me pass the day in peace, let me pass the night in peace... Under thy hand I pass the day, under thy hand I pass the night, thou art my mother, thou my father.')

May 17, 1841, aged ~22), Otshu Aga (from Urgeza in Sibu, who also transmitted songs from Bilile / Mahbuba of Guma, d. Oct. 27, 1840), and Aman Gonda (from Hibi in Goma, belonging to the wadjo / watcho subdivision of the Boranna sect, son of an aba fuño judicial officer) / Autonyms: oromo (pl. oromoni, p. 24) & himata ('orthodox believer', contrasted with faqi [Falasha], wada, zidama [Christian], and awalini [Muslim], p. 200) / Sects: Boranna (subdivision wadjo, p. 147) vs. djarzo (p. 78)

entries.english: 15 Verbatim Galla Proverbs (Magmaga) in Tutschek's Dictionary (1844)
entries.translation: (1) 'afan agabudan kad'ad'u' ('Pray with an empty/fasting mouth', p. 3); (2) 'ati malⁱ bechta harka arabu male' ('What knowest thou but to lick off the hand?', p. 9); (3) 'yo argite ebizi, yo d'abte abari' ('When thou receivest, bless; when thou dost not receive, curse!', p. 16); (4) 'ilkanin namni gitᵃumtu fira' ('By the teeth all men are friends — i.e., do not trust every smiling face', pp. 20, 121); (5) 'idya Wacᵃ kaba ura' & 'hadarinza kaba ura' ('The eye of God penetrates the wall' & 'His wisdom penetrates a wall', pp. 27, 190); (6) 'uma Wacayoti hinkolfin' ('Do thou not laugh at any of God's works!', p. 28); (7) 'ini aka kozi tȧ' ('He is like dung — i.e., as good and useful as manure', p. 37); (8) 'yo canqen gaya keza ut'ale namni indua' ('When a spark jumps out of the pipe, someone dies', p. 45); (9) 'ini aka gararati bifaza didirad'a' ('He changes his colour like a chameleon', p. 56); (10) 'Tchaba ati murte Naman bad'z'izin; — Liqi ati fud'te Naman bazizin' ('The wood which thou didst hew, let nobody carry; — The loan which thou didst take, let nobody pay', p. 72); (11) 'tchitinif ibida waliṅ gain; biçanif ibidi wali ha gau' ('Chaff and fire shall not come near each other; water and fire may approach each other', p. 74); (12) 'mukni Wacᵃ careṅ domu' ('The edge of the spear of God is not blunted', p. 102); (13) 'ibidif biçan hirmiṅ cabu, fulif gongon d'okzaṅ cabu' ('Fire and water have no prohibition, face and throat have no concealment', p. 114); (14) 'ini aka falʿanati afan nama dyala d'abad'a' ('He stands like a spoon under the mouth of men', p. 120) & 'madirati hinkolfini' ('Do not laugh during dinner', p. 162); (15) 'hodjad'z'u wayo mo tau wai?' ('Is it better to work or to sit idle?', pp. 146, 201), 'bokeṅi mit'ileṅ adjezu, zi adjeza?' ('The rain kills not even a little ant, will it kill thee?', p. 170), 'handangon qilenza ufiti naqeti ilman god'ad'a?' ('Does the hen lay eggs impregnated by the air?', p. 177), & 'namni ho bola lit'e hadaroma' ('When a man has fallen into the pit, he becomes wise', p. 190)

entries.english: 7 Verbatim Galla Songs (Wetu) in Tutschek's Dictionary (1844)
entries.translation: (1) 'Koromin wal ate, Latshu gugurod'a; — Nadeṅ wal arate, Latshu muzurod'a' ('Bulls gore, both are black; — Women altercate, both recently married', p. 1); (2) 'Ombo z'an bared'a, Maf baretu d'abe? Dyalalti d'ukuba, Maf arera d'abe?' ('Ombo z'an is handsome, why does he not find a fair maiden? Love is an illness, why does it not find medicine [arera]?', p. 10); (3) 'Wanin korriza, Muka cabad'a; Diarzi roriza, Durba kad'ad'a' ('The Wanin monkey growls and grasps a tree; the foolish bald-pate fellow means to win a maiden's heart', p. 36); (4) 'Galani na ñad'e, Giben na gezize; — Ano d'ufa djenan, D'iben na tezize' ('The river devoured me and carried me to the lake; — I said I shall come, but an obstacle detained me', p. 61); (5) 'Gaya t'ut'uko, Tambo na d'abi, Fag'afuftuko, Yambo na wami!' ('My pipe-smoker, put the tobacco here; my flute-player, call the dancers!', pp. 117–118); (6) 'Cotani cotani yaa babazani; Djed'ani djed'ani gargar nu bazani' ('They ploughed, ploughed and made a trench; they chattered, chattered and separated us', p. 127); (7) 'Zila zimalan yaba, Zimali dameṅ cabu; — Zila gandaran gala, Gandatu wareṅ cabu' ('In vain I climb a reed, a reed has no branches; — In vain I return to town, the town has no feeling for glory', p. 148) & 'Lenzan lon guza Bia gubati; D'enzan lon buza Iya nafati' ('Lenza grass causes cattle to dry up on the mountain; flight exposes cattle to screams of desperation', p. 158)

entries.english: Dr. Krapf's (1850, pp. viii–ix, 1–64) Dana River (Tana) Kigalla Dialect vs. Shoan Galla & Origin of "Ormania"
entries.translation: Studied in 1845 from Tana River Galla (Orma / Southern Oromo) near Takaongo and Berrarata to compare with his 1842 Shoan Galla vocabulary (10–12 degrees north) • Autonym & "Ormania" (p. ix): Coins "Ormania" ("an African Germania") from the Galla autonym Orma ("men / brave people"), correcting a French writer who confused Orma with morma ("neck") • Shared Amharic-Galla roots proved genuinely Cushitic/Galla because the Dana Galla have no contact with Christian Abyssinia • Greetings & Blessings (pp. 20, 24): nagaia bulte? ("good morning / hast thou passed the night in peace?") & wakne nágaia si kennu! ("farewell! may God give thee peace!")
entries.pronunciation: or-ma / or-ma-ni-a / be-rra-ra-ta / na-ga-ia bul-te / wak-ne na-ga-ia si ke-nnu
entries.context: Rev. Dr. J. L. Krapf (1850) 'Vocabulary of Six East-African Languages' (Tübingen), Preface pp. viii–ix & pp. 20, 24

entries.english: Dana River Kigalla Governance, Law, Religion & Nature Lexicon (Krapf 1850, pp. 1–64)
entries.translation: Religion & Priesthood: Wāka (God; soda Wakáti = godliness, p. 23), moru / bersíftu (wise man / priest / teacher, pp. 38, 63), kallu (soothsaying/divination, p. 47), bitta (sacrifice; bitta balfatje = to offer sacrifice, p. 42), kákăno / kákata (oath/covenant, pp. 12, 34), tába & makmáksa (story, fable, proverb, pp. 19, 39, 49) • Governance & War: móti / heiu (king/governor; mótuma / heiyóma = kingdom, p. 29), murra heiuáti (vice-regent, p. 60), subbo / abba duláti (general/commander, p. 22), nama ka yákamsu (judge; yákama = law/judgement, pp. 29–30), nágaia & arára (peace/reconciliation; ka arársu = mediator/peacemaker, pp. 33, 36) • Geography & Trade: Máro (Galla name for the Dana/Tana River, p. vii; gélăna = river, melka = ford, pp. 21, 41), mánia (sea; mánia gudda = ocean, pp. 34, 43), hówolo / hirrino (ship/canoe, p. 44), tjábi dakatjáti (snow/hail on mountains, p. 46), ilka arbu (elephant tusk / ivory traded to Pokomo and Swahili, p. vii & p. 29)
entries.pronunciation: wa-ka / mo-ru / ber-sif-tu / ka-llu / bi-tta / mo-ti / hei-u / su-bbo / a-ra-ra / ma-ro / ge-la-na
